ordinance_area_text: It shall be unlawful for any person to shoot any firearm in any areas of the County that are so heavily populated as to make such conduct dangerous to the inhabitants thereof, which areas are designated in Appendix J to the Fairfax County Code.
method: No official vector layer for Appendix J was found (searched ArcGIS Online, Fairfax County ArcGIS org services1.arcgis.com/ioennV6PpG5Xodq0, and www.fairfaxcounty.gov/mercator). The text of Appendix J itself could not be retrieved (Municode blocked). Built from the county's official Appendix J "No Shooting Areas" map PDF: rendered at 300 dpi, pink (restricted) and yellow (exempt) fills classified by color, raster georeferenced to the county outline in VA State Plane North (4-parameter similarity fit, median residual ~2.8 px ≈ 170 ft), vectorized; the yellow/pink dividing line was then snapped to TIGER 2023 centerlines of the roads labelled on the map wherever the traced line lay within 250 ft of them (~89% of its length): Leesburg Pike (SR 7), Towlston Road, Sully Road (SR 28), Braddock Road (SR 620), Ox Road (SR 123), Silverbrook Road (SR 600), Lorton Rd connector, Richmond Highway (US 1). Non-road portions (Towlston Rd/Georgetown Pike to the Potomac near Difficult Run; Accotink Creek, Accotink Bay and the east shore of Gunston Cove around Fort Belvoir) keep the traced map line. The county was split by this line and each face assigned to restricted/exempt by majority overlap with the traced map fills.
notes: Restricted area = pink "Areas where firearms and pneumatic guns may not be shot except as otherwise provided in Fairfax County Code Chapter 6" on the official map; roughly everything east of Sully Rd and south/west of Leesburg Pike, Towlston Rd, Braddock Rd, Ox Rd, Silverbrook Rd and Richmond Hwy, including Fort Belvoir main post. Share of county: 66.1%. Firearm discharge in the exempt area is still subject to Chapter 6: only on a "Parcel of Land" (per §6-1-1; the county wildlife page says 20 acres or larger) posted with signs; no hunting within 100 yards of primary/secondary highways; no slugs; .22-caliber limit except shotguns with multiple ball shot on exempt parcels; no shooting in/within 100 yards of public schools/parks. Accuracy: road-following segments use TIGER centerlines (±~10-20 m); non-road segments are traced from a letter-size county map (±~50-100 m). Towns of Herndon, Vienna and Clifton are colored on the map like their surroundings and are included (towns have their own ordinances). Cities of Fairfax and Falls Church are excluded by the jurisdiction outline. The map is dated November 2018; check for later amendments to Appendix J.
recovered: Recovered 2026-11 from public/data/local-areas.geojson (the original source files were lost); geometry carries that layer's 30% simplification.
